channel.title: Eid Alkhaldi - Blog
channel.description: Most teams can access the same models. My work is deciding what can be trusted, what must be verified, and how AI becomes an auditable system inside regulated Arabic-English workflows.

item.title: RPA for Brokers: Control Before Automation
item.description: Broker automation needs a control layer, not another set of screens wired together.

item.title: Fine-Tuning FLOPs as an AI Governance Signal
item.description: Compute accounting is becoming a governance record, not only an infrastructure metric.

item.title: MCP and the Future of Context Management
item.description: MCP should be understood as an interface discipline: it makes context and tools explicit enough to govern.

item.title: What Teams Get Wrong About MCPs in Production
item.description: MCP is useful only when teams treat context, tools, and session state as governed interfaces.

item.title: MCP Agents Need Session Integrity
item.description: The hard problem is not calling one tool; it is preserving meaning across a sequence of stateful tool interactions.

item.title: Why MCP Matters for Agent Infrastructure
item.description: MCP turns ad hoc agent integrations into contracts that can be tested, governed, and changed.

item.title: Gulf Enterprise Agents Need Closed-Loop Control
item.description: For Gulf enterprise agents, reliability depends on validating actions before they touch sensitive systems.

item.title: Fann or Flop: AI Agents Need Metered Reasoning
item.description: Agent quality will depend less on constant reasoning and more on deciding when extra reasoning is worth the cost.

item.title: Insurance AI Needs Reasoning-Grounded Retrieval
item.description: In insurance, high-risk errors usually come from weak grounding rather than weak language generation.

item.title: The Real Bottleneck in Gulf Arabic RAG
item.description: Arabic RAG failures frequently come from weak context assembly rather than weak embeddings.

item.title: Humility, Verification, and LLM Behavior
item.description: What looks like model humility is often an architecture that forces the system to pay for evidence.

item.title: Confidence Comes from Skipping the Evidence Loop
item.description: LLM confidence is less about model size and more about whether the system is forced to verify.

item.title: Why RAG Fails When Retrieval Is Not Evaluated
item.description: Many RAG failures are diagnosed as model failures even when the real error happened before generation.

item.title: Saudi Enterprises Are Wasting RAG Budget
item.description: The expensive part of RAG is not always the model. It is the absence of retrieval discipline.

item.title: Why Serious AI Teams Still Need Python
item.description: No-code orchestration can be useful at the boundary of a system, but it should not become the center of an AI engineering practice.

item.title: LLMs for Legal Compliance Need Memory
item.description: Compliance systems need institutional memory: how similar cases were interpreted, escalated, and resolved.

item.title: Arabic LLMs Need Evaluation That Understands Context
item.description: Arabic model quality should be judged by contextual behavior, not by fluency alone.

item.title: Arabic LLM Deployment Needs Semantic Evaluation
item.description: Arabic evaluation cannot stop at surface overlap; it must test whether meaning survives dialect, formality, and domain language.

item.title: Self-Evolving Agents Raise the Reliability Bar
item.description: Adaptive agents require stronger observability because the system that runs today may not behave exactly like the one tested yesterday.
